skills.content:
---
name: unclaimed-money-hunt
description: >-
  Use when searching official unclaimed-property sources for the owner's names
  and past addresses, or re-checking for new hits.
---
# Unclaimed money hunt

Inputs: the owner's name variants and every past address, read from their Vault contact entries. If missing, ask for every name variant (legal, middle, maiden, nicknames, business names) and every address, then save them to the Vault.

Source list: work through the unclaimed-money-sources skill in its search order. It is the source of truth for URLs, status, and scam signs.

## Fan-out order (start local, then widen)
1. Local: current city and county. City and county treasurer unclaimed-funds lists, excess-proceeds from tax sales, court registries. Download published PDF/CSV/XLS lists and search them for the last name.
2. Current state program (e.g. claimittexas.gov in Texas). Use the browser for the search form; page through all results.
3. Every other state lived in: that state's official program, plus an all-states sweep on MissingMoney.com (run by NAUPA). Always search Delaware too.
4. National: PBGC unclaimed pensions, FDIC and NCUA failed-bank deposits, HUD/FHA mortgage insurance refunds, US Courts unclaimed funds, VA life insurance, DOL back wages and abandoned plans, NAIC Life Insurance Policy Locator (owner-initiated only, explain), SEC, FTC and CFPB refund lists, IRS undelivered refunds (explain the path, don't log in).
5. Widen to nearby counties and cities from the address list until no new sources.

Keep a running ledger file of every source checked (date, URL, method, result: hit / no hit / blocked / needs sign-in or SSN) so re-checks skip duplicates and report only what's new.

## Output
Lead with the total found and the count of new hits. For each hit: source link, name and address as listed, holder, amount or range, claim steps and documents needed, and likely/possible from the name and address fit. Flag entries at the owner's address under other family names as family, not theirs. Say plainly which sources were blocked or need a sign-in or SSN. Never invent a hit or amount.

## Never
- File or submit a claim, enter an SSN or ID, upload documents, or create an account without the owner's explicit yes on that specific claim.
- Use or recommend paid finder or heir-locator services. Warn about look-alike scam sites; use only official .gov programs and MissingMoney.com.
- Email, text, call, or post anywhere.

## Re-check
Offer a monthly re-check routine; report only new hits.

skills.content:
---
name: Unclaimed money sources
description: >-
  Use when searching for someone's unclaimed money or property in the US: the
  verified list of official state, territory, federal and local sources, the
  order to search them, and the signs of a scam site.
---
# How to use
1. Start local: search the owner's current city and county (treasurer, district clerk registry, city unclaimed property), then their current state program.
2. Search every other state the owner has lived in, both on its own site and on MissingMoney. Hawaii and Guam are not on MissingMoney.
3. Always search Delaware too, because many corporations are domiciled there.
4. Search the federal sources. Any source that needs an SSN, a login, or a deceased person's details is listed for the owner to run; the bot never enters an SSN.
5. Widen to counties and cities near each past address, using the search pattern in section 4.
6. Log every source you checked, with or without a hit. Rows marked bot-blocked need the box browser, not a script fetch.

# Unclaimed money: official sources (US)

Verified: 2026-10-27, by automated HTTP check plus each agency's own page or search index.
Status key: **OK** = loaded (HTTP 200). **Redirect** = the old URL now forwards to the listed one; use the listed URL. **Bot-blocked** = the site refuses automated fetches but the URL was confirmed from the agency's own page or search index; open it in a real browser. **No online search** = the program exists but has no public search tool.
Rule: searching every source below is **free**. Never pay a fee, give a card, or use a "finder" to search.

## 1. Multi-state portals

| Source | URL | What it covers | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| MissingMoney.com (run for NAUPA, endorsed by states) | https://www.missingmoney.com/ | One search across 49 states (all but Hawaii), plus DC and Puerto Rico | Bot-blocked (Cloudflare 403). Real browser only |
| NAUPA / unclaimed.org | https://unclaimed.org/search/ | Directory linking to every state, territory and Canadian province program | OK |
| USA.gov unclaimed money hub | https://www.usa.gov/unclaimed-money | Federal hub linking to the federal sources in section 3 | OK |

## 2. State and territory programs (54)

MM = searchable on MissingMoney.com. Hawaii is the one state not on it, so also search each state's own site when an address ties to it.

| St | Program (agency) | Official search URL | MM | Status / notes |

| AK | Unclaimed Property (Dept of Revenue) | https://unclaimedproperty.alaska.gov/ | Yes | OK |
| AZ | Unclaimed Property (Dept of Revenue) | https://azdor.gov/unclaimed-property/owners-file-claim/search-for-property | Yes | OK. ADOR sends searches to MissingMoney |

## 3. Federal and national sources

| Source | URL | What it finds | Search needs | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TreasuryDirect Treasury Hunt | https://www.treasurydirect.gov/savings-bonds/treasury-hunt/ | Matured, uncashed savings bonds and held interest | SSN (owner runs it) | OK |
| TreasuryDirect: lost or destroyed bonds | https://www.treasurydirect.gov/savings-bonds/manage-bonds/lost-stolen-destroyed-ee-or-i-bonds/ | Replacing paper EE/I bonds (Form 1048) | Form | OK |
| PBGC unclaimed pensions | https://www.pbgc.gov/workers-retirees/find-unclaimed-retirement-benefits/search-unclaimed | Pensions from failed or ended defined-benefit plans | Name, employer | OK |
| FDIC unclaimed funds | https://closedbanks.fdic.gov/funds/ | Deposits from failed banks (move to the state after about 18 months) | Name | OK |
| NCUA unclaimed deposits | https://ncua.gov/support-services/conservatorships-liquidations/unclaimed-deposits | Deposits from liquidated credit unions | Name | OK |
| HUD/FHA refunds | https://entp.hud.gov/dsrs/refunds/ | FHA upfront mortgage insurance refunds (loans after Sep 1, 1983, paid off with no default) | Last name or FHA case number | OK |
| IRS refunds | https://www.irs.gov/refunds | Current refund status and lost-check traces | SSN (owner runs it) | OK |
| IRS undelivered refund (CP231) | https://www.irs.gov/individuals/understanding-your-cp231-notice | Refund checks returned as undeliverable | Notice | OK |
| USA.gov unclaimed tax refunds | https://www.usa.gov/unclaimed-tax-refunds | Plain-language guide to the IRS path | None | OK |
| SEC Fair Funds | https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/distributions-harmed-investors | Money from SEC enforcement cases | Find the case, then its administrator | Script-blocked; WebFetch OK |
| FTC refunds | https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/refunds | Consumer refunds from FTC cases | Per case | Bot-blocked; use the browser |
| CFPB payments to harmed consumers | https://www.consumerfinance.gov/enforcement/payments-harmed-consumers/payments-by-case/ | Payments from CFPB cases | Per case | OK |
| NAIC Life Insurance Policy Locator | https://eapps.naic.org/life-policy-locator/ | Life policies of a **deceased** person, for beneficiaries | The deceased's SSN and dates (owner runs it) | Bot-blocked. Free |
| DOL Abandoned Plan Search | https://www.askebsa.dol.gov/abandonedplansearch/ | 401(k)s abandoned by their sponsor | Plan or employer name | OK |
| DOL Retirement Savings Lost and Found | https://lostandfound.dol.gov/ | Old employer retirement plans | Login.gov (owner runs it) | OK |
| DOL Workers Owed Wages | https://webapps.dol.gov/wow/ | Back wages DOL couldn't deliver | Name, employer | OK |
| VA life insurance unclaimed funds | https://insurance.va.gov/UnclaimedFunds/Search | Unclaimed VA life insurance proceeds | Name | OK |
| US Courts Unclaimed Funds Locator | https://ucf.uscourts.gov/ | Unclaimed funds in federal bankruptcy courts | Name | OK. Claims go to the specific court (Form 1340) |
| Interior Dept IIM accounts | https://www.doi.gov/ost/iim-accounts | Individual Indian Money accounts | Contact OST | OK. Tribal-member beneficiaries only |
| National Registry of Unclaimed Retirement Benefits | https://www.unclaimedretirementbenefits.com/ | Retirement balances left with employers | SSN (owner runs it) | Bot-blocked. Legit and free (listed by PBGC), but private, so a match is only a lead |

## 4. Local patterns (county, district clerk, city)

Money that never reaches the state:
- **County treasurer:** small unclaimed amounts (in Texas, $100 or less), usually as a PDF list on the treasurer's page.
- **District clerk court registry:** court-held money such as tax-sale **excess proceeds**, judgments and interpleader funds. In Texas the former owner must petition within 2 years of a tax sale.
- **City unclaimed property:** uncashed city checks, utility deposits and vendor refunds.
- In Texas, county and city items over $100 go to the Comptroller, so search ClaimItTexas too.

Verified Texas examples:

| Place | Office | URL | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Texas | Comptroller: ClaimItTexas databases | https://www.claimittexas.gov/app/ucp-databases | OK |
| Travis County | Treasurer: unclaimed property | https://www.traviscountytx.gov/treasurer/unclaimed-property | OK |
| Travis County | District Clerk: court registry (excess proceeds) | https://www.traviscountytx.gov/district-clerk/finance-division/court-registry | OK |
| Williamson County | Treasurer: unclaimed property | https://www.wilcotx.gov/922/Unclaimed-Property | Script-blocked; WebFetch OK |
| Comal County | Treasurer: unclaimed funds | https://www.comalcounty.gov/379/Unclaimed-Funds-with-Comal-County | OK |
| Burnet County | Treasurer | https://www.burnetcountytexas.org/1401/Treasurer | OK |
| City of Austin | Search unclaimed property | https://www.austintexas.gov/services/search-unclaimed-property | OK |
| City of Austin | Open data: unclaimed property | https://data.austintexas.gov/Budget-and-Finance/Unclaimed-Property/h3i4-5e5v | OK |

To widen to another place, search "<county> county treasurer unclaimed funds", "<county> district clerk registry excess proceeds" and "<city> unclaimed property", and use only .gov or official county and city domains.

## 5. Scam warnings

Searching every official program is always free, and so is claiming directly from the state.

Signs of a fake or paid finder site:
- It charges a search, processing or release fee, or a subscription.
- It asks for a card, a bank login or gift cards.
- It wants a full SSN before it will show any match.
- It uses a look-alike domain. Get official URLs from unclaimed.org or the state treasurer. A few real ones aren't on .gov (lacashclaim.org, and vendor portals on *.unclaimedproperty.com and *.findyourunclaimedproperty.com linked from the state's .gov site).
- It pressures you with "expires today" or an amount you can't verify. Unclaimed property usually has no deadline. Tax-sale excess proceeds are the exception (2 years in Texas).
- It reached you by unsolicited email, text or call.
- It's an heir finder or asset locator asking for a percentage. You can always claim it yourself for free.

Bot rules: never pay, never enter an SSN or card, and never sign up with a finder without the owner's explicit yes. Report the claim link and let the owner file it.

---
name: finders-keepers-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for Ducat$' first conversation with a new owner, to collect names and
  addresses and start the first hunt.
---
# Getting started (Ducat$)

I find unclaimed money held for you by official state, county, city, and federal programs, and tell you how to claim it. I never file anything without your yes.

1. Check the Vault for the owner's contact entries. If names and addresses are there, confirm them in one line and skip to step 4.
2. Ask, in one message: every name you might be listed under (full legal name with middle, nicknames, maiden names, business names).
3. Then ask: every address you've lived at, as far back as you can remember, including out-of-state ones and any ZIP you're unsure of. Save each address to the Vault as its own contact entry (label like "Past address (street)").
4. Start the hunt right away with the unclaimed-money-hunt skill and the unclaimed-money-sources list, starting with their current city, county, and state. Send a short opener naming where you're starting.
5. When the first results are delivered, offer a monthly re-check routine that reports only new hits; create it on their yes.
